To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iron perturbation regulates the IFN‐γ response at multiple levels.
iron regulates IFN‐γ pathways by interfering with signal‐transduction mechanisms, resulting in transcriptional and posttranscriptional changes in IFN‐γ inducible gene expression.

iron modulates the IFN‐γ pathway in human monocytes by transcriptional and/or post‐transcription regulation of the IFN‐α/γ‐inducibile genes ICAM‐1 (CD54), HLA‐DR (HLA‐DP,DQ,DR) and GTP‐cyclohydrase‐I (GTP‐Ch).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of iron‐responsive genes in human monocytes and macrophages.
the role of iron in the regulation of IFN‐γ induced genes in human monocytes.
the regulation of IFN‐γ induced genes by iron and its possible role in the pathogenesis of iron deficiency anemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iron regulates IFN‐γ pathways by transcriptional as well as post‐transcription mechanisms.
iron‐regulated IFN‐γ pathways are controlled by iron at the transcriptional and post transcriptional level.
iron is a regulator of IFN‐γ signaling pathways, which is a novel finding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

iron regulates IFN‐γ signaling by affecting the expression of the IFN‐γ receptors and the expression of the downstream signaling molecules, the transcription factors, the transcriptional activity of the transcription factors and the posttranscriptional regulation of the IFNγ induced genes.

iron‐induced changes in IFN‐γ expression are due to a transcriptional regulation, whereas changes in IFNγ‐induced gene expression are caused by a combination of transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms.
IFN‐γ is a proinflammatory cytokine that can induce the expression of ICAM-1, HLA-DR, and GCH in human monocytes and that these responses are regulated by iron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iron can modulate IFN‐γ signaling pathways.
iron regulates IFN‐γ signaling by transcriptional and/or post‐transcription mechanisms, which are independent of the IFN‐γ receptors.
